answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Not yet, on either. Next week is about 24 mi, all easy, and four short strides on Thursday are the only faster running.

Your easy heart rate is already back to normal, so your fitness is fine. Muscles and tendons take longer to recover from a marathon, though, and a week ago stairs were hard. Tripling your mileage and adding speedwork in the same week is how injuries after a marathon usually start.

The Thanksgiving 10K still fits well. If it is on Thu Nov 26, the weeks could build like this:

| Week | Miles | Faster running |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 26 – Nov 1 | about 24 | strides only |
| Nov 2 – 8 | about 28 to 30 | strides and one light fartlek |
| Nov 9 – 15 | about 32 | one 10K session |
| Nov 16 – 22 | about 32 to 35 | one 10K session |
| Nov 23 – 26 | short runs | a few strides, race Thursday |

You don't need 40 mi for a 10K. Your marathon base carries you, and the sessions bring the speed. Tell me in your check-in whether you are racing it, and whether there is a spring marathon after that.

new.analysis:
## How last week went
You ran the recovery week exactly as planned. The 3, 4 and 5 mi runs landed on Wednesday, Friday and Sunday, and the four rest days stayed rest days. Nothing was skipped or overrun, and the only miss was the strength session.

## Recovery signs
Every marker is moving the right way. Pain stayed at 0, you felt better on each run, and the blister has healed.

| Run | Pace | Avg HR | Felt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wed Oct 21, 3 mi | 10:49/mi | 128 | 5/10 |
| Fri Oct 23, 4 mi | 10:16/mi | 133 | 7/10 |
| Sun Oct 25, 5 mi | 9:51/mi | 139 | 8/10 |

Your heart rate only rose because your pace did. Sunday's 9:51/mi at 139 matches your easy runs from before the race, so your aerobic fitness has not slipped.

## Why the build is gradual
Your fitness comes back faster than your legs do. Muscles and tendons usually need three to four weeks to repair after a marathon, even when nothing hurts. Going from 12 to 24 mi gets you most of the way back to the 30 mi you ran before this build, and that is a big enough step for one week.

## Why strides and strength now
The strides lead into the 10K work. They bring back quick, relaxed leg speed without the strain of a full session, so your legs are ready for a fartlek the week after. Strength matters for the longer term: your quads gave out late in the race, and stronger quads are the cheapest fix before your next marathon.

## What the race showed
Your pacing was right, but your build got cut short. You held 8:30/mi through 20, which was on track for about 3:43, before your quads faded. Moving the race earlier left room for only one 20-miler and no 22, and building that endurance is what your next marathon build should add.
